standard_prerequisites.name: Decomposition of a closed subscheme into its largest Cartier divisor and a residual part of codimension two
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, the lemma describing the codimension one part of a closed subscheme
standard_prerequisites.use: Decomposes the ideal sheaf of the given subscheme as a product of the ideal of its largest effective Cartier divisor and the ideal of a subscheme supported in finitely many points.

standard_prerequisites.name: Making an ideal defining finitely many points invertible by blowups in closed points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma producing a sequence of blowups in closed points after which an ideal supported on finitely many regular surface points becomes invertible
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the sequence of blowups making the residual ideal invertible, which is what makes the inverse image of the whole subscheme an effective Cartier divisor.

core_obligations: Split off the Cartier part (proof lines 4427-4438): the largest effective Cartier divisor contained in the given subscheme defines an ideal containing the ideal of the subscheme with quotient supported in closed points, so the ideal of the subscheme is the product of the ideal of a residual subscheme supported set theoretically in finitely many closed points with the ideal of that Cartier divisor.

Make the residual ideal invertible (proof lines 4438-4445): the principalization lemma gives a sequence of blowups in closed points along which the residual ideal becomes invertible; then the inverse image of the whole subscheme is locally defined by a product of an invertible ideal with the transformed Cartier divisor, hence is an effective Cartier divisor.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the ideal of the subscheme into a Cartier part and a part supported in finitely many points.
Apply the principalization lemma to the residual part.
Conclude that the inverse image of the subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a proper closed subscheme of a regular surface becomes an effective Cartier divisor after a sequence of blowups in closed points (statement lines 4423-4431). The proof (proof lines 4432-4445) splits off the largest effective Cartier divisor contained in the subscheme and principalizes the residual ideal supported in finitely many points. H2: a complete two step argument.
